extracted.intended_audience: first-time Wattpad writers / aspiring Wattpad creators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, platform-specific guidance for drafting, planning, and publishing a writer's first Wattpad story — covering ideation, titling, synopsis, goal-setting, drafting habits, editing strategy, and audience-building on Wattpad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flesh out your ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture and expand the ideas you keep returning to — free write to get ideas on paper without editing yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set a timer for 15 minutes and free-write all ideas; no idea is off limits. Afterwards, step back and highlight or circle the ideas you really love. Free writing helps get creative juices flowing and narrows down top ideas. If you have no ideas, try using prompts to get started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an inspiring title
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick a title that evokes feeling and keeps you tethered to your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about titles of favorite stories and what they evoke. The title doesn't have to be final — it serves as a placeholder to help focus you and make the project feel 'real'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write your synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a short, high-level synopsis that contains your main ideas and serves as a guideline for writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A synopsis can be brief and somewhat vague; it’s not an in‑depth draft. It can (and often should) change over time. The purpose is to keep you focused on the core of your story as you write.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set writing goals for yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete writing goals to stay motivated and break the project into manageable tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals help keep your sights on the project and maintain momentum by breaking the process into small, easy-to-accomplish tasks. Your end goal is to complete a story, but set interim milestones (daily/weekly word counts, chapter targets, deadlines) to make progress steady and measurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start small — and not at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a manageable scene or section rather than forcing the opening; choose a story structure that works for you and build outward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't need a wild event on page one to hook readers; big early spectacles can be hard to sustain. Strong beginnings often come after finishing the story when you know your characters and world. Consider writing out of sequence (start in the middle) — like movies, stories are often written nonlinearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow your story to change as you write — be willing to remove or add subplots, characters, or elements that don't serve the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an idea isn't working, don't be afraid to scrap an entire subplot or character, or to add new material. Flexibility lets the story evolve naturally and often improves the final result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't edit while you write
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid self-editing during the initial drafting phase to preserve creativity and forward momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing while drafting can stifle natural creativity; take the pressure off and focus on getting the first draft down. Save rigorous editing for after you complete your draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn how to build a captivated audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop readership by pairing a compelling story with consistent publishing and community engagement on Wattpad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key actions: ensure your story is unique and compelling; update frequently; perform a thorough edit to remove grammar/spelling errors; keep chapters to an easy-to-digest 1,500–2,000 word count (ideal); tag your story accurately so readers can find it. Also personalize your Wattpad profile, follow other Wattpadders, engage with favorite stories, and start conversations to connect with readers — readers come for the story and often stay because they love the writer.
